title: GORGO: Online Tuning for Cross-Region Network-Aware LLM Serving
technique: Cross-region proxy router scoring each replica by weighted network RTT + queue (tokens in flight) + uncached-prefill cost; the two weights are tuned online by a (1+1) evolution strategy whose fitness is rolling-window p95 TTFT

optimized_metrics.evidence: GORGO proxy uses a simple (1+1) evolutionary strategy to tune weights Wrtt and Wqueue on the objective function, p95 TTFT.
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: evolutionary strategies guide the GORGO policy's parameters to directly optimize p95 TTFT. ; The fitness function is the negative p95 TTFT (in seconds) of the rolling 128-request tuning window

headline_claim.text: we fix the parameter values learned from tuning and improve p95 TTFT by 6.9–15.5% and p95 end-to-end (E2E) latency by 14.3–30.9% over baseline loadbalancing policies such as simple session affinity and prefix-cache.

reported_metrics.where: Table 2, 3, 4 (headline p95 E2E gain is NOT an optimized objective: tuner optimizes p95 TTFT only; Limitations: it trades 'E2E and ITL tails for TTFT')
Table 4 input tok/s (offered load, not an outcome)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: TTFT is known to consist of three different costs: network latency, prefill time, and queueing delay [He et al., 2025].
metric_definitions.notes: TTFT includes client-proxy-to-replica network RTT, queueing and prefill (uncached tokens only): TTFT = Tnetwork(i) + Tqueue(i) + Tprefill(xr \ ci) (Eq. 1). Measured at the proxy so includes WAN RTT.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: tune GORGO's weights online to minimize the p95 TTFT of a rolling 128-request window with hop size 32
metric_definitions.notes: Fitness is computed over a rolling 128-request window (hop 32), so the optimized quantity is a windowed p95, lower than the whole-window p95 in Table 2.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Queued requests to the proxy are defined as recently dispatched requests without a token response
metric_definitions.notes: Tqueue input is the total tokens of requests without a completion event on the proxy, not the engine's queue.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Table 2 reports TTFT, E2E latency, and inter-token latency (ITL) for all policies in all three windows.
metric_definitions.notes: E2E and ITL never defined; ITL reported as median only.

load_regime: trace replay of ART-Chat-2.5M (Mooncake format timestamps) with time_scale 1.0/2.0/3.0 to vary saturation; BFCL replay with 128 concurrent episodes
tradeoff_acknowledged: Optimizing p95 TTFT can exploit continuous batching by concentrating load on the nearest replica, trading E2E and ITL tails for TTFT (Table 8 'reward hacking': wqueue=0 wins every TTFT percentile but is worst on E2E and ITL tails; p95 TTFT 17% better than next-best).
hardware: 3 regions (us-ashburn, eu-frankfurt, ap-seoul), 2x L40S each; BFCL: 2x H200 replicas
workloads: ART-Chat-2.5M (synthetic from production metadata, long-context high prefix reuse), WildChat-4.8M (appendix), BFCL multi-turn
extractor_notes: TAIL IN OBJECTIVE: yes - the ES fitness is negative rolling-window p95 TTFT (single-statistic, tail objective). p95/p99 E2E improvements are reported only; E2E demoted from objective. Paper itself documents reward hacking of the p95 TTFT objective (Appendix D / Table 8). Load classed online-arrivals (timestamped trace replay, time-scaled); BFCL part is closed-loop concurrent episodes. Not a Vidur/simulator study; real multi-region deployment.
load_class_quote: The trace follows Mooncake's FAST'25 format [Qin et al., 2025] containing per-request timestamps, which can be linearly scaled to simulate variable saturation profiles.
